summary: We did not find a dated dog event for this weekend, so these are dependable spots where you can meet other dog owners. Heads up: David H. Ready Dog Park is closed until December 23, and we could not confirm the Demuth Park dog parks have reopened after construction, so call the city before you go.
heatNote: Late November highs in Palm Springs are expected to be in the 70s, comfortable for dogs, but afternoons can feel warm and wind can pick up. Bring water, and recheck the forecast closer to the day.

picks.name: Boozehounds brunch
picks.when: Friday to Sunday, brunch 10 am to 3 pm
picks.where: 2080 N. Palm Canyon Drive, Palm Springs
picks.why: A restaurant built around dogs and their people, so the tables around you are full of fellow dog owners.
picks.check: Hours differ a little between listings, so confirm brunch hours and ask about a dog friendly table. 760 656 0067.

picks.name: 4 Paws Coffee Co.
picks.when: Saturday and Sunday morning (listings show roughly 7 am to 3 pm)
picks.where: 2500 N. Palm Canyon Drive, Suite A5, Palm Springs
picks.why: A neighborhood coffee shop centered on dogs and community, where dogs are welcome on the outdoor patio and conversations come easily.
picks.check: Listed hours conflict, so call to confirm before you go. Keep your dog leashed. 760 832 8021.

picks.name: Palm Springs Air Museum
picks.where: 745 N. Gene Autry Trail, Palm Springs
picks.why: A fresh outing where friendly dogs on a leash are welcome, with plenty of visitors to chat with.
picks.check: Ask about loud engine runs or demonstrations before bringing a noise sensitive dog. 760 778 6262.

picks.name: Whitewater Preserve
picks.where: Whitewater Preserve, about 25 minutes northwest of Palm Springs
picks.why: Leashed dogs are allowed on the preserve trails, and cool fall mornings are ideal for a hike where you will likely cross paths with other dog owners.
picks.check: Confirm weekend hours with the Wildlands Conservancy, keep your dog on a leash, and check wind in the pass before you drive out.
